title: What If You Got Lost In A Forest?
sources: US Forest Service and National Park Service lost-hiker guidance: stop, stay where you are, and signal; staying put makes you easier to find
Three blasts of a whistle is the widely taught distress signal (Scouting and park safety guidance)

lines.say: What would you do if you got lost in a forest?
lines.cap: What would [you] do / if you got [lost]?

lines.say: The sun is going down, and every tree looks the same.
lines.cap: The sun is [going down] / every tree / looks the [same]

lines.say: Wandering around makes you much harder to find,
so stay right where you are.
Step two: be loud and bright.
Three blasts on a whistle is the classic call for help.
lines.cap: [Three] blasts / on a whistle / call for [help]

lines.say: Step three: keep warm, and wait.
Searchers find people who stay put.
